nodes.task: Read input/operations.csv from the mission working directory using file_list and file_read only, verify its structure and row count, and independently recompute all operations metrics from the raw integer records: per-team and overall work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, schedule_variance_minutes (actual minus planned), completion_percent (completed/work_orders x100) and minutes_per_completed_order (actual/completed). Round only at final serialization, to exactly two decimal places, from unrounded raw arithmetic. Persist the result as metrics.json with root keys row_count, totals, teams in that order; teams in the order Atlas, Birch, Cedar; each totals/team object containing exactly work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order, schedule_variance_minutes in that order and no extra fields. All integer metrics must be JSON numbers with no decimal point; completion_percent and minutes_per_completed_order must serialize with exactly two decimal places. Use the already-given expected values only as a cross-check after your own computation, and report any mismatch explicitly instead of forcing the numbers to match.

Read the persisted metrics.json produced by the analyst delegation and input/operations.csv, then write operations-brief.md containing: a concise executive recommendation; exact overall and per-team findings for completion, defects and schedule variance derived only from input/operations.csv and the verified metrics; and a Method section that names input/operations.csv explicitly and states the exact formulas completed/work orders x100, actual/completed minutes, and actual minus planned minutes. Every number quoted must match the persisted metrics.json exactly, using the same two-decimal formatting for completion_percent and minutes_per_completed_order. Keep conclusions limited to the supplied six-week three-team dataset and draw no causal claims beyond the data.
